correctness.rationale: The coin-count decomposition N=aT+2j, J=j+ka, t=T-2k is exact because a is odd. The bounded-partition lemma is proved by base-case counts and zero/three padding inductions with endpoint uniqueness. All j=0,1,2 and j>=3 thresholds account for every k>=0, and the maximal threshold comparison is strict for a>=9. Monotonicity by adding the smallest coin lifts the Apéry maxima to the unrestricted Frobenius formula. Exact DP verifies 97 odd parameter cases, but it is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The fixed-four-denomination three-representation threshold and its complete next Apéry layer for all odd a>=9 are not implied by the first (two-representation) layer in Mohammed (2017, Chapter 6), the three-generator formulas in Komatsu--Ying (2023), or Komatsu--Hyun--Song (2026) whose odd progression blocks grow in length with their least generator. Their only four-generator parameter-linked blocks have least terms 5 or 7, both outside the new domain. Searches for the equivalent at-most-two / at-least-three formulation and the fixed arithmetic progression detected no covering published theorem.
residual_risks: An equivalent formula could exist in an unindexed or inaccessible work; no database exhausts all prior publications.
